impact_assessment.why: IDEA-1209 was approved: page reads were cut silently with a marker and screenshots had no ceiling, so a caller could not tell a cut element from an absent one.
impact_assessment.benefits: A missing element is unambiguous; a caller can narrow scope or opt into a reported truncation; the image payload is bounded.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: the three read methods gain optional arguments and get_html can now return success=false; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Truncation is only implicit when the caller opts in, the refusal names the scope and budget it measured, and existing callers receive an explicit receipt instead of a silent cut.

impact_assessment.why: IDEA-1237 was approved: outcomes were bare dicts, so a flow or tool result could not be joined to the step that produced it.
impact_assessment.benefits: Outcomes carry trace and parent-span identity; sampling is decided once per trace; untraced behaviour is byte-identical.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: emit_outcome may add three keys and TraceContext gains fields; dependency: stdlib contextvars only; concurrency: contextvar isolation; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: The caller's dict is copied, never mutated, and a failing provider only logs at debug.

impact_assessment.why: IDEA-1238 was approved: prompt text had no version, digest or label, so a rollout was an in-place edit and a rollback meant finding old prose by hand.
impact_assessment.benefits: Two runs are comparable by (name, version) or digest; a rollout is a label move; a rollback is one audited operation.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new module and state shape; dependency: stdlib hashlib/json; concurrency: in-memory, caller owns persistence; state: explicit JSON export.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Empty prompts, unknown versions and the reserved 'latest' label are refused with Why/Fix; state round-trips in tests.

impact_assessment.why: IDEA-1242 was approved: a delegated task had no capability bound, expected output or recursion limit.
impact_assessment.benefits: A parent states what a delegatee may do and what shape to return; an out-of-contract tool is refused before acting; recursion is bounded.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new module; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: The contract is data the runtime must pass down, validation needs only task id and role, and a missing schema accepts any output for old callers.

impact_assessment.why: IDEA-1243 was approved: a handoff was a plain dict with no delivery record, acceptance check or retry, so a rejected one vanished silently.
impact_assessment.benefits: Delivery and acceptance are distinct, a failed handoff is retried or visibly exhausted, and context is bounded before it reaches a prompt.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new module; dependency: stdlib dataclasses only; concurrency: in-memory; state: packets serialise with as_dict.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Caps are enforced at construction, a raising check rejects rather than crashes, and an empty schema-free accept is an explicit opt-out.
